cover.title: Why Is Baby Formula So Expensive?
cover.label: Formula

lines.text: Four companies made about 90% of America's baby formula.
lines.say: Four companies made about ninety percent of America's baby formula.

lines.text: That was 2022. The CPI for baby food and formula rose 31% from 2020 to 2025.
lines.say: That was in twenty twenty-two, and the price index for baby food and formula rose thirty-one percent from twenty twenty to twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: The worst year: +11.6% in 2022, after a recall at Abbott's Michigan plant emptied shelves.
lines.say: The worst year was twenty twenty-two, up eleven point six percent, after a recall at Abbott's Michigan plant emptied shelves.

lines.text: Imports face US tariffs of up to 17.5%, and were only about 2% of US formula in 2022.
lines.say: Imports barely compete: they face US tariffs of up to seventeen and a half percent, and were only about two percent of US formula in twenty twenty-two.

lines.text: WIC picks one brand per state. GAO found the winner's shelf price rose 1.7%, about 30¢ a 12-oz can.
lines.say: Then there's WIC, the biggest formula buyer, which picks one brand per state, and the GAO found that the winning brand's shelf price rose one point seven percent, about thirty cents a twelve-ounce can.

lines.text: The surprise: every infant formula sold in the US must meet the same FDA nutrient rules, store brands included.
lines.say: Here's the part that surprises people: every infant formula sold in the US must meet the same federal nutrient rules, store brands included.

lines.text: Example: a 12-lb baby drinks about 30 oz a day, or 900 oz a month. At 12¢ vs 25¢ an ounce: $108 vs $225.
lines.say: For example, a twelve-pound baby drinks about thirty ounces a day, or nine hundred a month, so at twelve cents versus twenty-five cents an ounce, that's one hundred eight dollars versus two hundred twenty-five.

lines.text: Same federal nutrient rules, $117 a month apart in this example.
lines.say: Same federal nutrient rules, one hundred seventeen dollars a month apart in this example.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.ig:
Four companies made about 90% of America's baby formula in 2022.
The US price index for baby food and formula rose 31% from 2020 to 2025, including 11.6% in 2022 alone.
Imports face tariffs up to 17.5% and were about 2% of US formula in 2022. GAO found WIC contract winners' shelf prices rose 1.7%.
Every infant formula sold in the US must meet the same FDA nutrient rules, store brands included.
Sources: FTC, BLS, CRS, GAO, FDA, AAP.
